intro: Luxembourg rewards visitors with free public transport, a walkable old town, and easy access to nature. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Tram T1 connects the airport to the city centre and Gare, every 8 minutes, free.
Buses 1-31 serve the city; most stop at Hamilius and Gare, free.
Taxis are available but limited; ride apps like Uber and Bolt operate.
Driving is easy but parking in the centre is paid and scarce on weekends.
Walking and cycling are great; the city is compact and bike-friendly.
No ferries; the country is landlocked.

palace.name: Grand Ducal Palace
palace.price_text: Check on the day; guided tours in summer only, fee varies
palace.hours: Exterior always viewable · guided tours usually mid-July to early September, check on the day
palace.tip: Book a summer guided tour early; otherwise come for the changing of the guard, which is short and free.

casemates.name: Bock Casemates
casemates.price_text: ≈ EUR 7–9 adult, reduced for children; check on the day
casemates.hours: Usually daily spring–autumn, shorter hours in winter; check on the day
casemates.tip: Wear shoes with grip and bring a light layer; the tunnels are cool and uneven.

corniche.name: Le Chemin de la Corniche
corniche.tip: Walk it slowly at golden hour; the view over the Grund is the classic Luxembourg photo.

cathedral.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral, Luxembourg
cathedral.hours: Usually open daily, roughly 08:00–18:00; check on the day
cathedral.tip: Step inside quietly during services and look up at the crypt below.

adolphe.name: Adolphe Bridge
adolphe.tip: Walk across for the best view down into the Pétrusse valley, then take the path below.

gaardebounen.name: Judd mat Gaardebounen (dish)
gaardebounen.price_text: ≈ EUR 18–28 in a traditional restaurant; check on the day
gaardebounen.hours: Served at lunch and dinner in most traditional restaurants
gaardebounen.tip: Try it at a classic city restaurant; it is smoked pork with broad beans, hearty and filling.

mudam.name: Mudam Luxembourg
mudam.price_text: ≈ EUR 10–14 adult; check on the day
mudam.hours: Usually closed Monday; check on the day
mudam.tip: The building by I. M. Pei is as good as the art; allow time for the terrace view.

parc-merveilleux.name: Parc Merveilleux
parc-merveilleux.price_text: ≈ EUR 6–10 entry; check on the day
parc-merveilleux.hours: Seasonal, usually spring–autumn; check on the day
parc-merveilleux.tip: A short train ride from the city; good with children and for the fairy-tale figures.

place-guillaume.name: Place Guillaume II (Knuedler)
place-guillaume.tip: The main square for a coffee stop; markets and events run here through the week.

grund-walk.name: Grund old town walk
grund-walk.tip: Take the lift down from the city and wander the riverside lanes; it feels like a village.

petrusse.name: Pétrusse valley walk
petrusse.tip: A green path under the bridges; go down from the Adolphe Bridge side.

city-train.name: City tourist train (Pétrusse Express)
city-train.price_text: ≈ EUR 10–14 adult; check on the day
city-train.hours: Seasonal, usually spring–autumn; check on the day
city-train.tip: A quick way to see the upper and lower town if you have limited time or limited mobility.

market.name: Place d'Armes food and flower market
market.price_text: Free to browse; pay per item
market.hours: Usually weekend mornings; check on the day
market.tip: Come early for fresh produce and a pastry; the square is full of cafés after.

kirchberg-view.name: Kirchberg plateau viewpoint
kirchberg-view.tip: Combine with Mudam and the Philharmonie; the modern quarter is a contrast to the old town.

gare-walk.name: Gare district walk
gare-walk.tip: The station area is practical for food and shops; walk toward the centre for the old town.

philharmonie.name: Philharmonie Luxembourg
philharmonie.price_text: Ticket prices vary by concert; check on the day
philharmonie.hours: Performance times vary; box office daytime
philharmonie.tip: Check the programme online; even the foyer architecture is worth a look.

fort-thungen.name: Fort Thüngen (Dräi Eechelen)
fort-thungen.price_text: Free entry to the museum; check on the day
fort-thungen.hours: Usually closed Monday; check on the day
fort-thungen.tip: Quiet fort museum near Mudam; good for the city's fortress history without crowds.

moselle-tour.name: Day trip to the Moselle wine region
moselle-tour.price_text: ≈ EUR 15–30 for transport and tastings; check on the day
moselle-tour.tip: Take the train to Remich or Wasserbillig and taste local wines along the river.

chemin-rail.name: Chemin de la Corniche to Grund stairs
chemin-rail.tip: Link the corniche to the Grund on foot for the best half-day loop in the city.

casemates-petrusse.name: Pétrusse casemates (if open)
casemates-petrusse.hours: Seasonal, often summer only; check on the day
casemates-petrusse.tip: Smaller and quieter than the Bock Casemates; confirm opening before you go.

chocolate-house.name: Chocolate House café
chocolate-house.price_text: ≈ EUR 5–12 for a drink and spoon chocolate; check on the day
chocolate-house.hours: Usually daily daytime; check on the day
chocolate-house.tip: A sweet stop near the palace; good for a quick local treat.

three-towers.name: Three Towers (Dräi Tierm) walk
three-towers.tip: Short walk along the old ramparts; combine with the Bock area.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: UNESCO walls, casemates and WWII memory.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Valley walks, parks and the Grund below the city.

stays.why: Inside the old town: walk to the Bock, casemates and Grand Ducal Palace. Quiet at night, few budget rooms.
Around the main station: most hotels, best value, free tram and buses to the centre in minutes.
Modern business district with big hotels and museums; good for parking and the EU quarter.
The old lower town in the valley: pretty, quiet and close to nightlife; steep walk or lift up to the centre.

food: Try Luxembourgish classics: judd mat gaardebounen (smoked pork with broad beans), gromperekichelcher potato fritters and bouneschlupp soup.
Look for a 'Kniddelen' or 'Mettwurst' lunch in the old town; portions are big, so share.
Place d'Armes and the Grund have the densest café and restaurant clusters; book dinner on weekends.
Cheap eats: bakery sandwiches, kebab and Asian lunch spots near the Gare, roughly EUR 8–15 a meal.
Wine and beer are local: try a Moselle wine or a Luxembourgish craft beer. Prices in the centre are high, so compare menus.
more_time: Day trip to Vianden: castle and river valley, roughly an hour by train and bus; check connections on the day.
Add a half-day to the Moselle wine villages (Remich, Grevenmacher) by bus or car.
History fans can swap a museum for the American Military Cemetery in Hamm or the Schueberfouer fair if it is on.
